name: Question 8
problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=4-{t}^{2}$, where $t>0$ is the time  in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s},$ calculate the maximum velocity ${v}_{\text{max}}$ of the particle and determine the time when the particle reaches its maximum velocity.
worked_solution:
The extrema of the velocity $v$ occur at the critical points of $v.$

Since $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=a(t),$ to find the times where $v$ is a maximum, we just need to solve $a(t)=0$ and test each solution using the first or second derivative test.

Solving $a(t)=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =0 \\ 4-{t}^{2} & =0 \\ (2-t)(2+t) & =0 \\ t & =\pm 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t⩾0$, the extremum of the velocity function occurs when $t=2\,\text{s}.$

We now test the extreme value using the second derivative test. For this, we find the second derivative of $v(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}^{″}(t) & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}v}{\text{d}{t}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(a(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4-{t}^{2}) \\  & =-2t \\ {v}^{″}(2) & =-2(2) \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${v}^{″}(2)<0,$ we conclude that the velocity is maximized when $t=2\,\text{s}.$

Now, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (4-{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =4t-\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)-\frac{1}{3}(0)^{3}+C & =0 \\ 0+0+C & =0\,⟹\,C=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=4t-\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}.$

Finally, we calculate the maximum velocity:

$$
{v}_{\text{max}}=v(2)=4(2)-\frac{1}{3}(2)^{3}=\frac{16}{3}\,\text{m}/\text{s}
$$

Question 8
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=4−t2, where t>0 is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=0m/s when t=0s, calculate the maximum velocity vmax of the particle and determine the time when the particle reaches its maximum velocity.

a
vmax=163m/s,t=2s
b
vmax=83m/s,t=2s
c
vmax=113m/s,t=1s
d
vmax=13m/s,t=1s
e
vmax=143m/s,t=2s
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The extrema of the velocity v occur at the critical points of v.

Since dvdt=a(t), to find the times where v is a maximum, we just need to solve a(t)=0 and test each solution using the first or second derivative test.

Solving a(t)=0 gives

a(t)=04−t2=0(2−t)(2+t)=0t=±2.

Since t⩾0, the extremum of the velocity function occurs when t=2s.

We now test the extreme value using the second derivative test. For this, we find the second derivative of v(t) and evaluate it at t=2:

v″(t)=d2vdt2=ddt(dvdt)=ddt(a(t))=ddt(4−t2)=−2tv″(2)=−2(2)=−4.

Since v″(2)<0, we conclude that the velocity is maximized when t=2s.

Now, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫(4−t2)dt=4t−13t3+C To determine C, we use the fact that v(0)=0. Substituting this into the above gives 4(0)−13(0)3+C=00+0+C=0⟹C=0. Therefore, the velocity v of the particle at time t is v(t)=4t−13t3.

Finally, we calculate the maximum velocity:

vmax=v(2)=4(2)−13(2)3=163m/s
